title: Interacted with a hotel personnel and they told me nothing there is real, but an AI program
content: In my previous post about the hospital for terminal patients, I mentioned a blue-grey hotel. Recently, I visited it again, but this time there was a twist—the hotel (or hotels) seemed to be endless. I initially checked into a different hotel, and once again, everything was impeccable—luxurious finishes, exquisite furniture, and exceptionally well-trained staff. The hotel was bustling with people, each absorbed in their own business. It was a modern, minimalist space, characterized by plenty of glass walls and curtains. As I wandered through the corridors, I unexpectedly came across another reception area behind automatic doors. Curious, I approached, and a lady at the desk informed me that I could check into this new hotel without any extra effort. “Because all of this is the same,” she explained, “there are many more like it.” This hotel had a distinct style—an enchanted garden vibe. I agreed, and she checked me in. As I continued to explore, I discovered many different hotels along the corridors, including the familiar blue-grey one. The hotel was, indeed, endless. During my stay, I went to the beach at night. It was lively, with many people bathing in the high waves. I sat and observed until something felt off—particularly the sky, which didn’t appear “natural.” Puzzled, I went to the reception and asked about it. The receptionist smiled and replied: “Oh, that’s AI. Nothing here is real. Don’t you remember? It’s been a very long time since we merged, and now we live here.” I then asked where our real bodies were. She explained that a massive hangar had been built, connecting continents—either over or under the oceans (I didn’t quite catch that part). We are there, sleeping, while the program runs.
